title: Composable runway templates for Hosted API + Model Catalog: sprint orchestration & eval guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Repeated cross-team friction during quarterly planning shows up as: inconsistent canary windows, missing evaluation sets for model swaps, and ad-hoc capacity hedges. That increases risk for hosted API model rotations and leads to downstream incidents when rollouts collide with capacity spikes.

Goal: Create a set of composable sprint/runway templates that PMs and Eng leads can instantiate for any hosted API + model catalog lane. Each template should encode: milestone cadence (canary -> ramp -> full), required eval test matrix, capacity hedge thresholds, rollback criteria, and an OKR-linked KPI set so roadmap items are measurable.

Scope: Deliver a template library (three opinionated templates: Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive), a one-click checklist for Console/Runbook creation, and an accompanying PRD + Confluence playbook with sample mappings to existing Hosted API model catalog lanes. Templates must integrate with canary scheduling, release windows, and evaluation harness hooks (end-to-end smoke tests, quality regression metrics).

Non-goals: This ticket does not modify runtime scheduling or autoscale code. Operational changes needed after template adoption will be captured as follow-up ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Three template variants (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive) documented in Confluence with example timelines and owner roles
Template JSON schema that can be imported into the Console to pre-populate rollout fields (fields: canary_duration, evaluation_sets, capacity_thresholds, rollback_criteria, okr_kpis)
Confluence playbook with 5 example lane mappings from current hosted model catalog and at least 2 worked examples for Dedicated lanes
Design mockups (Figma) for one-click 'instantiate template' flow reviewed and approved by DX
Pilot: run two model rotations using Balanced template with automated evals and no customer-impacting regressions for 48h after full ramp
